author: nero_eth
content:
If we ship EIP-8411, we should ensure that we're able to separate BAL from payload (directly or later on).
This halves the objects size (at 276M gas we cross 8 MiB payloadEnvelope size, at 345M, we cross 10 mib), and it allows to introduce an earlier BAL availability deadline later on.
Fundamentally, BAL and txs are different and shouldn't be put kept in the same object, with the same rules applied to both of them.
Here's a PR how this could work with EIP-8411:
https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12535

author: nero_eth
content: 8146 was, but 8411 is Fast Execution Payload Broadcast.

author: nero_eth
content:
tbf, I'm proposing this. Not deciding we do it, and I only do so to make sure we can safely scale beyond 300M if we wanted in hegota.
It's fine if we end up not doing it, and ELs can also ship data repricings to prevent big payloads hitting limits already at 300M, but taking out the BAL would just be a simple halving of payload sizes.

author: .paulharris
content: we do need things in the spec before devnets because theres testing implications on that, and an unstable PR vs 'in the spec' is an important distinction, especially when we're changing things as we pull them from their EIP form to be in a hard fork.

author: tersec
content: Yeah, agree with this, specs are how the interop is decided. There's some set of interoperable implementations that have to exist, with test vectors etc etc

author: .paulharris
content: i do concede it'd be better to have client devs looking at things before merge, so if thats the main reason for that comment above then, yeh i do agree with that bit, but in terms of working on open prs, im not a huge fan of that idea

author: potuz
content: In the specs doesn't mean in the fork branch. There's test vectors and everything you need for testing on feature branches

author: .paulharris
content: in the case of quick slots the implementation is changing in the pr going to heze. i think the CFI's going into alpha/beta releases with tests is ultimately what we have been doing, and what we should continue to do. things should be moving into 'heze' as we decide the feature is going onto a devnet, and devnets should be based on a release of the spec, otherwise we're just adding points to make life difficult for no value.
